shortDescription: Metallic rattling, buzzing, or sitar-like notes when fretting or playing open strings.

q_location.title: Buzz Location
q_location.question: Where does the fret buzz happen most noticeably on your guitar?
q_location.measurementGuide: Play notes chromatically up each string with normal picking force. Note where the buzz is clearest.

options.label: Open strings only (frets 0)
options.description: Buzzes when plucked open, but goes away immediately when you press any fret.

options.label: Low frets (Frets 1 to 5)
options.description: Buzzes primarily on chords and notes near the headstock.

options.label: Upper frets (Frets 12 and above)
options.description: Buzzes high up the neck or chokes out when bending notes.

options.label: One specific note / fret only
options.description: All other notes ring clearly, but one individual fret buzzes or dies out.

options.label: Everywhere along the entire neck
options.description: General rattling on almost every fret across all strings.

q_open_details.title: Open String Buzz Test
q_open_details.question: Does placing a folded strip of paper or business card in the nut slot temporarily stop the buzz?
q_open_details.measurementGuide: Slide a tiny slip of paper under the buzzing string at the headstock nut, re-tune, and pluck gently.

options.label: Yes, the buzz disappears or improves
No, it still buzzes at the bridge or tuner hardware

q_low_frets.title: Neck Relief Check
q_low_frets.question: When you fret the 1st fret with your left index finger and the last fret with your right pinky, is there a small gap under the string at the 7th fret?
q_low_frets.measurementGuide: Use a standard plastic credit card or business card at the 7th–8th fret as a feeler gauge. There should be a hair of space (approx 0.25mm - 0.35mm, about the thickness of a business card).

options.label: No gap at all — the string touches the 7th fret wire firmly (Backbow)
Normal gap (business card slides through), but frets 1-3 still buzz

q_high_frets.title: Bridge Saddle Height & Upper Relief
q_high_frets.question: How high are your strings above the 12th fret wire without pressing down?
q_high_frets.measurementGuide: Place a ruler on top of the 12th fret wire. Standard low-medium electric action is around 1.5mm - 2.0mm (approx thickness of 1 to 2 standard guitar picks).

options.label: Strings are lower than 1.2mm (very close to frets)
Normal action height, but notes choke out during bends past fret 12

q_single_fret.title: Fret Level Rocker Test
q_single_fret.question: Does a short straightedge (like the edge of a credit card bridging only 3 frets) rock back and forth over the buzzing fret?
q_single_fret.measurementGuide: Spanning exactly 3 frets with a rigid edge. If it rocks like a seesaw, the center fret is high.

options.label: Yes, it rocks distinctly over the fret directly ahead
No rocking, but there is a visible indentation or groove in the fret wire

q_all_frets.title: Overall Action & Tuning Environment
q_all_frets.question: Did this buzz start suddenly after a season/humidity change or changing string gauges?
q_all_frets.measurementGuide: Check if strings were down-gauged (e.g. 10s to 9s which decreases tension) or weather became dry.

options.label: Yes, recently changed strings or weather changed drastically
No change, guitar has simply become unplayable everywhere

nut_slot_too_low.title: Nut Slot Cut Too Deep or Worn Down
rankedCauses: Nut slot wear from string friction over time
Nut slot filed too aggressively during a previous setup
String gauge swapped to a thinner diameter that sits too deep in the slot
fixOrder: Temporary check: Place a tiny strip of folded foil or paper under the string in the nut slot.
Quick fix: The 'baking soda + thin superglue' or bone dust drop method to build up the slot floor, then re-file carefully with a needle file.
Permanent fix: Replace the nut with a pre-slotted Graph Tech TUSQ or bone nut.
measurementsRequired: Fret the string between the 2nd and 3rd frets. Check clearance over the 1st fret: you should see a tiny gap (about 0.15mm, thickness of a sheet of printer paper).
nut_slot_too_low.whenToConsultLuthier: If you don't own proper nut slotting files, cutting a new nut from a blank requires precision tools to prevent intonation problems.

truss_rod_too_tight.title: Truss Rod Over-Tightened (Neck Backbow)
rankedCauses: Truss rod has too much tension, causing the neck to bow backward toward the strings
Drop in ambient humidity causing fingerboard shrinkage and neck pull
Down-tuning or installing lighter gauge strings with less pull against the rod
fixOrder: Identify truss rod location (headstock or neck heel).
Loosen the truss rod by turning Counter-Clockwise (lefty-loosey) by exactly 1/8 to 1/4 of a turn.
Retune to pitch and let the wood settle for 15-30 minutes.
Re-check low fret clearance with the credit-card / business-card feeler test.
measurementsRequired: Capo on fret 1, hold down fret 17. Measure gap at fret 7. Ideal relief: 0.25mm - 0.35mm (standard business card).
truss_rod_too_tight.whenToConsultLuthier: If the truss rod nut feels completely stuck, does not turn with gentle pressure, or spins freely without gripping.

bridge_saddles_too_low.title: Bridge Saddles Set Too Low
rankedCauses: Bridge height adjustment screws vibrated lower over time
Action was set too low in pursuit of easy fretting without accounting for string vibration arc
fixOrder: Loosen the buzzing string slightly to reduce tension on the saddle screw.
Use the appropriate hex wrench (usually 1.5mm or 0.050") to raise both saddle height screws by 1/4 to 1/2 turn clockwise.
Tune to pitch and check frets 12-21 again.
Match the bridge saddle curvature to the fretboard radius.
measurementsRequired: Height from top of 12th fret wire to bottom of string: 1.6mm (High E) to 2.0mm (Low E) for standard electric.
bridge_saddles_too_low.whenToConsultLuthier: If bridge saddles are already raised to their maximum limit and string action is still too low (indicates neck angle issue requiring a neck pocket shim).

high_individual_fret.title: High or Unseated Fret Wire
rankedCauses: Fret wire popped out of its slot due to wood contraction in dry weather
Uneven factory fret leveling
fixOrder: Inspect the fret end near the fretboard edge to see if it has lifted out of the slot.
If lifted: Support the neck underneath, protect the fret with a brass punch or wooden block, and tap gently to re-seat it.
If fully seated but still high: Mark fret top with dry-erase marker and level/crown using a fret leveling file.
measurementsRequired: Fret rocker test across 3 frets: center fret should have zero rocking motion.
high_individual_fret.whenToConsultLuthier: Fret dressing, leveling, and recrowning requires dedicated crowning files and crowning guards to avoid creating dead spots.

worn_fret_grooves.title: Deep Fret Wear Grooves
rankedCauses: Thousands of hours of string bending in favorite positions (commonly frets 1-3 for open chords or 12-15 for blues bends)
fixOrder: Check fret height: if frets have sufficient remaining height (> 1.0mm), a partial or full fret level, crown, and polish will restore smooth playability.
If frets are worn down almost to the wood (< 0.7mm), a partial or complete refret is required.
measurementsRequired: Visual inspection under direct light showing divots or flat-topped trapezoidal fret crowns.
worn_fret_grooves.whenToConsultLuthier: Refretting is a specialized workshop procedure.

loose_hardware_bridge.title: Sympathetic Hardware Vibration
rankedCauses: Loose tuner ferrule or washer buzzing against headstock
Saddle intonation spring rattling
Pickguard screw or pickup height spring loose
fixOrder: Touch various hardware parts (tuning pegs, bridge springs, truss rod cover) while plucking the open string.
When the buzzing stops upon touching a specific part, tighten that specific screw or place a drop of foam/tape underneath.
loose_hardware_bridge.whenToConsultLuthier: Rarely needed unless a bridge casting has an internal hairline fracture.

fretboard_fallaway_or_radius.title: Upper Fret Rise or Radius Choke
rankedCauses: The neck joint area (where neck bolts/glues to body) has swollen or risen slightly higher than the rest of the neck (fretboard tongue rise)
Vintage 7.25" fretboard radius choking out high whole-step string bends
fixOrder: Slightly raise the bridge saddle of the choking string.
Introduce a tiny amount of neck relief loosening the truss rod 1/8 turn.
For vintage radius guitars: slightly higher action above fret 12 is physically required to clear bent strings.
measurementsRequired: Test full step bends on frets 12, 14, 15 on High E and B strings.
fretboard_fallaway_or_radius.whenToConsultLuthier: Adding deliberate fallaway (shaving frets 15-22 slightly lower on the treble side) is a standard luthier setup procedure.

nut_slot_uneven_or_low_relief.title: Insufficient Neck Relief Combined With Low Nut
rankedCauses: Neck is too straight (nearly zero relief) combined with aggressively cut nut slots
fixOrder: Loosen truss rod 1/8 turn counter-clockwise to allow the natural string tension to create a gentle forward curve.
Retune and check frets 1 through 5.
measurementsRequired: Target 0.25mm (0.010 inch) neck relief at fret 7.
nut_slot_uneven_or_low_relief.whenToConsultLuthier: If relief is correct and 1st fret still buzzes on one string.

tension_drop_season_shift.title: Seasonal Humidity Shift / Tension Drop
rankedCauses: Winter heating dried out the guitar neck, flattening or backbowing the fingerboard
Switching from heavier to lighter string gauge
fixOrder: Inspect case humidity (aim for 45% - 55% RH).
Perform a 1/4 turn truss rod adjustment (counter-clockwise to add relief).
Let guitar acclimate for 24 hours in a humidified environment.
tension_drop_season_shift.whenToConsultLuthier: If acoustic guitar top has sunken significantly from dry climate.

full_setup_needed.title: Comprehensive Setup Required
rankedCauses: Multiple interacting parameters out of spec (truss rod, nut slots, saddle radius, and intonation)
fixOrder: Follow the standard four-step setup order (T-R-A-I):
1. Tune to pitch.
2. Relief: adjust truss rod to 0.25mm at fret 7.
3. Action: adjust bridge saddles to 1.6mm - 2.0mm at fret 12.
4. Intonation: adjust saddle length so open note equals 12th fret harmonic.
measurementsRequired: Ruler (mm/64ths), business card/feeler gauge, accurate electronic tuner.
full_setup_needed.whenToConsultLuthier: If you prefer a professional bench setup or if fret leveling is suspected.
